newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil forecasters predict cold weekend for coffee.
newsitem.headline: Brazil forecasters predict cold weekend for coffee.

text.p: Brazilian weather services were forecasting a cold weekend for the country's key coffee regions, with temperatures possibly dropping to critical levels.
The reason for the anticipated sharp fall in temperatures is a polar air mass which is arriving overland and therefore carries more impact, forecasters said.
The air mass is expected to have a center of high pressure of 1,020 millibars which is weak "but it is coming in dry and cold," said Marcos Massari of independent meteorologists Somar.
Both Somar and National Institute of Meteorology (Inmet) anticipate temperatures dropping markedly in the early morning of June 8.
Temperatures in the Cerrado region of Minas Gerais and north Sao Paulo state could fall to between three and six degrees Celsius early Sunday morning, said Somar's Massari.
"In the Cerrado region, there is a possibility of light frosts in low-lying areas but these would not be frosts that hit coffee," Massari said.

In Pocos de Caldas, south of Minas and traditionally Brazil's coldest coffee area, cloud cover will prevent temperatures falling too sharply on June 8 but then skies should clear, with the early morning of June 9 expected to be the most critical, he added.
Much depends on a low pressure system which is currently sending wet winds across the region, Massari added.

"If the low pressure system moves out to the ocean, we could have frost conditions. But if it stays, the humidity means that we would be free of frost and there would only be cold. For the time being it looks as if it is staying," he added.
The north Parana coffee region should be protected by cloud cover throughout this time.
For the time being, Inmet does not expect to see any frosts in the coffee regions because of the weakness of the air mass.
"For the moment, we cannot confirm any possibility of frost, only that temperatures will fall sharply," a forecaster said.

A forecaster at National Institute for Space Studies expected temperatures to drop from the early morning of June 7 particularly in the Sao Paulo region and did not rule out the possibility of frosts although he pointed out that any outlook at this stage was only a tendency and not a forecast. ((-Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151))
